editorial_changes: Removed the i² explanation in Theorem 1.2.2 and used g in G to invoke ad-bc=1. Removed the named Euler-formula explanation in Proposition 1.2.3.

Introduced the search for invariant Riemannian geometry before defining path length, distance and area. Rotations at i force scalar Euclidean tangent coefficients; the affine position map forces the height factor y^-2.
Added Proposition 1.3.1 with complete proofs of metric uniqueness, induced area, and uniqueness among smooth positive area densities, including verification of invariance.
Normalized the tangent vector 1 at i to have length one and derived area from perpendicular length scaling. Explicitly distinguished the square-root scaling of lengths from the scaling of area.
Retained all previous Section 1.3 semantic labels and later geodesic/Laplacian content; the normalized metric definition is now 1.3.2.

Added a clearly linked stronger Radon-measure uniqueness theorem in Section 1.8, with a complete proof using horizontal translations, dilations, and a logarithmic change of coordinates. No abstract Haar uniqueness or circular dependency is used.
Updated the existing tangent inner-product and metric/area entries in the 63-entry notational index.

new_formal_claims.label: hyperbolic.mobius

new_formal_claims.label: hyperbolic.metric
new_formal_claims.scope: Positivity of normSq(v)/y² for nonzero complex tangent vectors.

new_formal_claims.label: hyperbolic.metric
new_formal_claims.scope: Squared tangent length agrees with the Euclidean norm squared at i.

new_formal_claims.label: hyperbolic.invariance
new_formal_claims.scope: Squared tangent length is preserved by the actual fractional derivative; no path-distance claim.

new_formal_claims.label: hyperbolic.invariant-geometry
new_formal_claims.scope: A field of symmetric positive-definite real bilinear forms invariant under the actual derivative has coefficients c Re(v conj(w))/y² with c>0. Smoothness is unnecessary for this uniqueness direction; no manifold bundle construction is claimed.

new_formal_claims.label: hyperbolic.invariant-geometry
new_formal_claims.scope: The density 1/y² satisfies the pointwise squared-derivative covariance law.

new_formal_claims.label: hyperbolic.invariant-geometry
new_formal_claims.scope: Every positive function satisfying that covariance law is C/y², with C>0; the measure/change-of-variables bridge remains open.

proof_correspondence: The bilinear uniqueness proof follows the prose: the derivative of k(pi/4) is i; invariance and symmetry remove the mixed coefficient; the derivative of s(x+iy) transports the base form.
The derivative theorem uses the complex quotient rule and determinant one. The density classification evaluates covariance at i using s(x+iy).
The tangent statements use real bilinear forms on complex coordinates. The later L² product remains complex and linear in its first argument.
